summary.overview: Apple reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16% year-over-year, marking a June quarter record. Tim Cook highlighted strong growth led by iPhone and Mac segments alongside positive early feedback for Siri AI beta testing. Kevan Parekh provided September quarter revenue growth guidance of 9%-11%, noting significant memory cost inflation and supply constraints.
keyTakeaways: Tim Cook announced this as his final earnings call, with John Ternus stepping in as incoming CEO.
September quarter total revenue is expected to grow by 9%-11%, impacted by a 2.5 percentage point FX headwind and advanced node and memory supply constraints.
Memory costs increased significantly in the June quarter and are expected to be even higher in September due to exponential increases from a 100-year flood.
Siri AI public beta feedback has been overwhelmingly positive, with potential compute costs managed via iCloud+ upgrades.
The EU commission is coordinating with Apple for Siri AI rollouts, while China approval to ship original Apple Intelligence features was received.
financialHighlights: June quarter revenue reached $109.4 billion, representing a 16% increase year-over-year.
Company gross margin expanded to 50.1%, up 80 basis points sequentially, while products gross margin reached 40.1%.
Diluted earnings per share were $2.02, up 29% from a year ago on net income of $29.8 billion.
Operating expenses totaled $19.1 billion, up 23% year-over-year.
Services revenue reached $30.7 billion, up 12% year-over-year with a gross margin of 75.6%.
guidance: total company revenue growth year-over-year: 9%-11% for the September quarter
iPhone reported growth rate year-over-year: mid-teens for the September quarter
gross margin: 47%-48% for the September quarter
operating expenses: $19.1 billion-$19.4 billion for the September quarter
other income and expense (OIE): around $350 million for the September quarter
tax rate: around 16.5% for the September quarter

qa.question: Can you discuss how much of the September revenue decel is supply constraint versus FX, and address memory cost inflation and sourcing flexibility?
qa.answer: Kevan Parekh stated that September revenue is expected to grow by 9%-11% impacted by a 2.5 percentage point FX headwind and significantly increased supply constraints. On memory, higher costs in June and September are partially offset by carry-in inventory and lower non-memory component costs.

qa.question: Can you discuss expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program, and share learnings from the iOS 27 and Apple Intelligence public beta regarding Siri AI and compute costs?
qa.answer: Tim Cook stated that early feedback for the Apple Upgrade Program is quite positive and that beta feedback for Siri AI is overwhelmingly positive, with compute costs potentially offset via iCloud+ upgrades.

qa.question: How do supply constraints impact the December quarter following the September guidance, and can you broaden out silicon providers to alleviate constraints?
qa.answer: Tim Cook stated that primary supply issues involve advanced nodes for SoCs due to demand outperforming expectations, noted they do not provide guidance beyond September, and added that the Arizona fab is ramping well.

qa.question: Is it your intention to pursue multi-year LTAs with suppliers for memory, and what is your pricing philosophy to protect product gross profit dollars versus margins? Also, what drove services deceleration and what are the moving pieces for 4Q services?
qa.answer: Tim Cook stated they reluctantly raised prices due to a 100-year flood on memory pricing and evaluate pricing across units, revenue, and margin over the long term. Kevan Parekh added that FX, lack of a theatrical release, and mobile gaming headwinds drove services deceleration, with a 5 percentage point FX headwind expected in September.

qa.question: What are your updated thoughts on the timing and hurdles for launching Siri AI in China and Europe, and can you walk through the sequential gross margin drivers for September?
qa.answer: Tim Cook stated that in the EU they are working with the commission while Mac gets Siri AI immediately, and in China they received approval for original Apple Intelligence features last week. Kevan Parekh added that memory cost changes explain the sequential gross margin change from June to September.

unanswered.question: How do supply constraints impact the December quarter following the September guidance?
unanswered.how: declined to provide guidance beyond the September quarter

guidanceRevisions: Total company revenue growth guidance moved from 14% to 17% year-over-year for June to 9%-11% for September.
Gross margin guidance moved from 47.5%-48.5% for June to 47%-48% for September.
Operating expenses guidance moved from $18.8B-$19.1B for June to $19.1B-$19.4B for September.
Other income and expense guidance moved from around $250M for June to around $350M for September.
Tax rate guidance moved from around 17% for June to around 16.5% for September.
whatChanged.toneShift: The language shifted to address severe external headwinds like memory cost inflation and supply constraints, alongside the historic announcement of Tim Cook's final earnings call and John Ternus succeeding him.

risksMentioned: Significantly increased supply constraints affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad driven by advanced nodes for SoCs
Exponentially higher memory costs characterized as a 100-year flood on memory pricing
Foreign exchange headwinds impacting September revenue growth by 2.5 percentage points and services by 5 percentage points
Regulatory hurdles in the EU and China for rolling out Siri AI

exchanges.question: Logistical question about question limit and opening the call to the operator.
exchanges.answer: Thank you, Tim. We ask that you limit yourself to two questions. Operator, may we have the first question, please?

exchanges.question: Can you discuss how much of the September revenue decel is supply constraint versus FX, and address memory cost inflation and sourcing flexibility?
exchanges.answer: We expect September total revenue to grow by 9%-11% impacted by a 2.5 percentage point FX headwind and significantly increased supply constraints affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad. On memory, we paid significantly more in the June quarter and expect even higher memory costs in September, partially offset by carry-in inventory and lower non-memory component costs.

exchanges.question: Can you discuss expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program, and share learnings from the iOS 27 and Apple Intelligence public beta regarding Siri AI and compute costs?
exchanges.answer: Apple Upgrade makes it easier for customers to get our latest products with a leasing plan, leveraging our high residual values, with early feedback being quite positive. We are off the charts excited about Siri AI with overwhelmingly positive beta feedback, and while compute costs are early, we believe some users will upgrade via iCloud+.

exchanges.question: How do supply constraints impact the December quarter following the September guidance, and can you broaden out silicon providers to alleviate constraints?
exchanges.answer: The primary supply issue is advanced nodes for SoCs driven by demand outperforming expectations rather than regular supply issues. We do not provide guidance beyond the September quarter, and our Arizona fab is ramping well as part of our U.S. commitments.

exchanges.question: Is it your intention to pursue multi-year LTAs with suppliers for memory, and what is your pricing philosophy to protect product gross profit dollars versus margins? Also, what drove services deceleration and what are the moving pieces for 4Q services?
exchanges.answer: We reluctantly raised prices due to a 100-year flood on memory pricing with exponential increases, and we evaluate pricing across units, revenue, and margin over the long term. For services, FX was the main sequential driver along with a lack of a theatrical release compared to last year and mobile gaming headwinds, and we expect a 5 percentage point FX headwind for September.

exchanges.question: Have you seen any pull forward of demand from consumers or enterprise, and does AI open up additional addressable markets over time?
exchanges.answer: iPhone has been running at 22% growth year-to-date and a pull forward is not obvious in the data, while price elasticity for iPad and Mac following price increases is too early to determine. There are enormous opportunities for Apple moving forward in AI, including the strategic advantage of on-device request processing.

exchanges.question: Will Siri AI change the capital intensity of Apple given hybrid cloud and on-device processing, and John Ternus, how do you see the competitive landscape evolving against new device entrants?
exchanges.answer: We use a hybrid model with third-party cloud and our own data centers, and while our OpEx and COGS have increased for AI, the balance of costs remains uncertain depending on iCloud plan upgrades. John Ternus added that there is immense opportunity in the space and we are focused on our plans.

exchanges.question: What are your updated thoughts on the timing and hurdles for launching Siri AI in China and Europe, and can you walk through the sequential gross margin drivers for September?
exchanges.answer: In the EU we are working closely with the commission to launch Siri AI, though it will be offered on Mac immediately as it is not covered by the same regulations. In China, we received approval to ship original Apple Intelligence features last week and are working on the Siri AI rollout. Kevan Parekh added that the sequential gross margin change from June to September is more than explained by memory cost changes.

exchanges.question: Can you evaluate the recent management changes and elevation of Doug and Troy to co-presidents, and what does it mean for your tenure as CEO?
exchanges.answer: The board made a decision to appoint two co-presidents to prepare them to do far more at the company. This has not changed the timetable for the CEO role. Marianne decided to retire upon knowing about the plans. On markets and investment banking sustainability, IB fees were fine by historical standards but not at super peak levels, and while there was some pull forward, the pipeline remains robust. Equities revenue was exceptionally strong and hard to repeat, but the background environment is supportive.

exchanges.question: What are the drivers of CCB deposit growth, and how does higher for longer impact the 15% retail market share goal? Also, where are we in the investment cycle and operating leverage outlook?
exchanges.answer: Wholesale deposit growth has outperformed expectations, partly driven by lending environment tailwinds. Consumer deposit growth expects low single-digit growth for the year, balancing strong checking account growth against yield-seeking flows. The 15% retail share is a long-term outcome of executing strategy. On expenses, the firm continues to invest aggressively for future returns while delivering exceptional current returns.

exchanges.question: What are the drivers of the upward revision to NII ex-Markets and its cadence, and what drives higher markets NII despite higher rates?
exchanges.answer: Full year NII ex-Markets is revised up from $95 billion to $96.5 billion, driven primarily by deposit balances across wholesale and consumer, plus slightly higher short and back-end rates. Markets NII is expected up due to changes in balance sheet composition expecting lower non-interest-bearing assets, and a $150 million shift from moving equity out of corporate into CIB.

exchanges.question: What characteristics are you and the board looking for in the next CEO, and is Marianne's departure an extension of your tenure?
exchanges.answer: The board-determined timing is essentially the same as previously stated. Desired CEO characteristics include management ability, analytical detail, being a culture carrier, curiosity, heart, grit, soul, work ethic, and flexibility to manage a global workforce. The firm has a deep bench of leaders, including COO Jen Piepszak and Mary Erdoes.

exchanges.question: Is there a time over the intermediate term where expense growth could slow and operating leverage becomes more likely? Any update on regulatory proposals like G-SIB surcharge and Basel III?
exchanges.answer: Operating leverage will not increase forever, and a slowdown in growth could occur in 2027 or 2028. On regulation, four changes should be made: do numbers correctly without false conservatism, remove the double count in operating risk capital, remove the double count in market risk capital, and adjust G-SIB and short-term wholesale funding rules to be fair.

exchanges.question: Is the current environment as good as it gets, and is there a tipping point where deposit behavior and betas change in a higher rate scenario?
exchanges.answer: Jamie noted it is getting close to as good as it gets, and the question is how long it lasts. On deposit betas, common sense suggests convexity kicks in eventually, and the firm models true stress tests with regime changes to account for potential acceleration in rate paid.

exchanges.question: How do you view operating leverage given revenue growth, and what gives you confidence that Troy is the right person to run the consumer business without prior consumer experience?
exchanges.answer: Operating leverage was positive, and rapid revenue increases drive big operating leverage. Regarding Troy, he has exceptional analytics, brain power, EQ, heart, and culture-carrying ability demonstrated across markets, investment banking, operations, and technology. Broad cross-company experience is beneficial.

exchanges.question: Can AI allow banks to operate with a much leaner structure and different organizational model? Also, what was most exceptional in equities this quarter?
exchanges.answer: AI will drive huge efficiency and is being used across nearly 1,000 use cases, but ultimate benefits accrue to customers in a competitive market. Jeremy Barnum added that equities strength was driven by headlines like major IPOs, index rebalancing, Korean market dynamics, and Asian activity, which are statistically improbable to repeat in exact combination.

exchanges.question: What is the health of the Main Street consumer and commercial lending? Also, why buy back stock at three times tangible book instead of keeping excess capital for a rainy day?
exchanges.answer: Consumer spend is robust across segments, delinquencies are lower than expected, and labor markets remain resilient. On capital, the firm intends to deploy capital organically at a 17% return, addressing enormous global infrastructure, defense, trade, and deficit needs, while remaining open-minded on inorganic M&A.

exchanges.question: What is the status and rollout timeline for the smart cash tool, and what are the European consumer banking aspirations?
exchanges.answer: The smart cash tool is a test case involving narrow customer segments, and something will be seen this year. On European consumer banking, digital expansion is succeeding in the U.K. with nearly 2.5 to 3 million customers, and Berlin has opened with better-than-expected progress, with the ultimate dream of building a pan-European digital bank.

exchanges.question: What are you seeing in credit underwriting standards among competitors, and can we enter a period of regulatory stability that enhances valuations?
exchanges.answer: Jeremy Barnum noted data center underwriting exhibits normal competitive pressures with some aggressive terms, while Jamie Dimon noted mild deterioration in revenue assumptions, add-backs, PIK, and covenants among some players. On regulation, Jeremy sees regulatory stability as a desirable, nonpartisan goal, and Jamie noted Supreme Court decisions and regulatory reflection could help establish a safer system.

exchanges.question: Are you pulling forward any tech or marketing spend given the environment, and how nimble do you expect CIB capital allocation to be?
exchanges.answer: Token expense is forecast for meaningful acceleration in the second half, though the full-year contribution remains trivial. On CIB capital allocation, it is driven by active client demand and passive effects like market risk and equity appreciation, and with excess capital, the firm can support clients where returns and risk appetite align.

exchanges.question: How does the consumer market evolve for aesthetic-driven approaches, and how unique or similar is the U.S. versus international self-pay market at this point?
exchanges.answer: Overall obesity utilization remains in the mid-single-digit range, leaving significant growth opportunity. In the U.S., about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions are self-pay, and efforts are ongoing to increase access, affordability, and consumer awareness through LillyDirect. Outside the U.S., the obesity business is mainly out of pocket, and consumer activation models are being replicated with regional regulatory adaptations.

exchanges.question: Why has the U.S. Foundayo launch been slower than anticipated, and what are the competitive dynamics and learnings from the OUS launch where competitors like Novo Nordisk are also scaling oral pills?
exchanges.answer: Foundayo progress involves physician education, access, and consumer awareness. Following CVS addition in June and the July 1 Bridge program, U.S. scripts are inflecting with volume nearly doubling in a month and about one out of four new starts on Foundayo. OUS, the UAE launch showed oral medicines expanding the market with combined incretin share holding steady despite competition.

exchanges.question: What are the requirements and milestones ahead for retatrutide to be accepted under the BLA pathway, and is this unique to retatrutide or applicable to subsequent incretins?
exchanges.answer: Lilly maintains retatrutide qualifies as a biologic application under amino acid count rules and protein analogy. Active litigation is ongoing, and Lilly hopes to conclude discussions with the FDA while gathering additional CMC data to support a BLA submission in Q1 2027.

exchanges.question: What are the early learnings and surprises from the Medicare Obesity rollout, and what is the ramp curve for orals versus injectables?
exchanges.answer: The Medicare Bridge program increases obesity access by 35% for seniors, showing a significant inflection point with smooth prior authorizations. Injectables account for about 80% of treatment preference, and 60% to 70% represent new patients who previously lacked access.

exchanges.question: Does retatrutide need a commercial strategy to protect against available compounded alternatives, and do its higher efficacy levels open up additional indications beyond tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: Patients are expected to vote with their feet for authentic retatrutide once available. The high dose provides transformative weight loss opening up indications like osteoarthritis knee pain, MASH, MASLD, and chronic lower back pain studies reading out next year.

exchanges.question: What is the post-Verzenio strategy in breast cancer regarding SERDs, oral PI3K, and an all-oral combination?
exchanges.answer: Lilly targets the estrogen receptor, CDK4/6, and PI3 kinase alpha. The strategy involves imlunestrant as INLURIYO with EMBER-4 reading out next year, and initiating phase III for tersolisib to combine with endocrine therapies and eventually with INLURIYO and Verzenio.

exchanges.question: Does the updated full-year guidance imply a deceleration in revenues for the back half of the year versus Q2, and is management being conservative?
exchanges.answer: The guide factors out prior-period adjustments for U.S. rebates and discounts occurring in Q2. Additionally, the second half of 2025 included a large bolus of international MOUNJARO launches that will not repeat, though dollar growth remains strong, alongside standard European Q3 vacation seasonality.

exchanges.question: Which specific OUS regions see the most growth, and what are the observations regarding generic semaglutide in India and other markets?
exchanges.answer: MOUNJARO OUS growth is led by China NRDL category leadership, Korea, the U.K., Mexico, and Germany. In India and Brazil, TRx for MOUNJARO continues to grow despite generic semaglutide due to superior clinical data, while generic manufacturers experience supply constraints.

exchanges.question: How extensive is the Foundayo sampling program, is it dampening IQVIA weekly prescription data, and what is the expansion of the U.S. prescribing base?
exchanges.answer: Sampling includes the first 30 days of initial dosing, similar to retail oral small molecules, supported by full supply. Prescribers have expanded from 8,000 to 36,000, showing continued week-on-week adoption and awareness.

exchanges.question: How sustainable is the medical exception delta driving net pricing, and how does CVS formulary placement impact favorable rebate adjustments quarter over quarter?
exchanges.answer: Medical exceptions are a short-term driver, but open access via CVS formulary placement starting in Q4 will reduce prices for patients. This expectation is fully embedded in guidance and offset by volume growth.

exchanges.question: Are psychiatry and vaccines areas Lilly can scale as high priorities, or are these assets more opportunistic one-offs?
exchanges.answer: These areas share immense unmet need, and acquisitions were made at prices permitting financial discipline and value creation. Lilly remains opportunistic based on available science and strategic fit.

exchanges.question: What specific pipeline products outside of obesity should the street pay more attention to?
exchanges.answer: Highlights include ASCVD gene editing for PCSK9, oral and injectable Lp(a) drugs, sleep-wake disorders from Centessa, oncology readouts including Kelonia in vivo CAR T for multiple myeloma and AJ1-11095 JAK inhibitor, and new indications and combination ideas in immunology.

exchanges.question: What is the potential for Foundayo ex-U.S. for obesity given UAE sales, and how will ex-U.S. governments reimburse Foundayo for diabetes compared to tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: While UAE start is strong, inventory builds play a role, and major rollouts occur in early 2027. Orals may be slightly better positioned for Type 2 reimbursement given head-to-head trial data, though OUS reimbursement always takes time.

summary.overview: Apple reported Q3 2026 revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16% year-over-year, driven by strong iPhone and Mac sales despite ongoing supply constraints. The impact from supply constraints is expected to increase significantly sequentially, affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad. The constraints are primarily driven by the availability of the advanced nodes that our SoCs are produced on.

exchanges.question: Could you talk a little bit about the expected adoption rates across your two and a half billion device install base in success? Do you see it shortening the replacement cycle for iPhone or also having an equal impact to Mac and iPad, which may have not have benefited from device subsidies in the U.S. like iPhone has historically?
exchanges.answer: The Apple Upgrade program is designed to make it easier for customers to get our latest products with a leasing plan that's right for them. It is offered in our retail stores and is not widely offered in all channels. We'll see what the customer uptake is, but the early feedback is quite positive. It is only available in the U.S. right now.

exchanges.question: Is there any guidance you can give us there as you see it, Tim, and we'd really appreciate it. Is there any possibility that you guys broaden out your silicon providers in a reasonable time frame to alleviate these so we feel better about supply?
exchanges.answer: The primary supply constraint is advanced nodes that we run our SoCs on, driven by a demand forecast issue where iPhone and Mac are doing remarkably better than expected. We are not providing any color or guidance beyond the September quarter. We do source over 100 million components this year out of Arizona, which is part of our $600 billion commitment to the U.S.

exchanges.question: Is it your intention to pursue some of these multi-year LTAs with your suppliers just to ensure access to supply at pre-agreed prices? When you approach product pricing in this environment, is it your intention to protect product gross profit dollars?
exchanges.answer: We reluctantly raised prices because we are in a 100-year flood on memory pricing with exponential increases. We look at units, revenue, and margin, and come to a business judgment as to how to handle that over the long term. We expect foreign exchange to drive about a 5 percentage point headwind to the year-over-year growth rate from the March to September quarter for services.

exchanges.question: I'm curious of how you assess whether or not you've seen any pull forward of demand, either from the consumer or even the enterprise and education markets. Do you see other kind of addressable markets evolving from AI over time?
exchanges.answer: It's not obvious in the data that there has been a pull forward of demand. We've had to increase prices on iPad and Mac, and it's too early to come to a definitive conclusion on price elasticity. There are enormous opportunities for Apple moving forward in AI, and the ability to run some percentage of requests on device is very strategic.

exchanges.question: Do you expect that Siri AI would change the capital intensity of Apple, despite the fact that you have the ability to do so much differentiated workloads on device, and you have this distributed compute? I'd love to get maybe a just a high-level take from you if you think that the competitive landscape here is changing.
exchanges.answer: We use a hybrid model with some third-party cloud and our own data centers. We have been growing our OpEx and spending more in AI in general. There is also the ability for people to move up on an iCloud Plan when they use it a lot. We are focused on our plans and very excited about the opportunity in this space.

exchanges.question: Just wanted to get your updated thoughts on that front and any more color in terms of what hurdles you need to cross to be able to launch it in those regions. Any way to walk us through the sequential driver there and how much of that is FX impacting it versus maybe increased commodity costs, et cetera, that's driving that sequential moderation?
exchanges.answer: We are working closely with the commission in the EU to try to get to a solution that would allow us to offer Siri AI there. It will be offered for the Mac there. In China, we received approval to ship the original features of Apple Intelligence and are working through the rollout. The sequential change in gross margin is more than 100% explained by the memory cost change.

summary.overview: Apple reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16% year-over-year, driven by record June quarter revenue in iPhone, Mac, and Services. Diluted earnings per share increased 29% to $2.02, supported by a 50.1% gross margin that included approximately two percentage points of benefit from tariff refunds. The call marked Tim Cook's final earnings call as CEO ahead of handing leadership to incoming CEO John Ternus.
keyTakeaways: Revenue grew 16% year-over-year to a June quarter record of $109.4 billion, led by a 22% increase in iPhone revenue to $54.3 billion and 29% growth in Mac revenue.
Gross margin reached 50.1%, aided by roughly two percentage points from tariff refunds, but Kevan Parekh, CFO, expects gross margins to moderate to 47% to 48% in Q4.
Supply constraints are expanding into Q4 to affect iPhone, Mac, and iPad, which Tim Cook, CEO, attributed to demand outpacing company forecasts rather than supplier failure.
Tim Cook, CEO, noted the company reluctantly raised prices to counter exponential memory price increases, which he characterized as a 100-year flood.
Tim Cook, CEO, confirmed this was his final earnings call, with incoming CEO John Ternus taking over earnings calls going forward.
financialHighlights: Total revenue reached $109.4 billion, an increase of 16% year-over-year.
Net income reached a June quarter record of $29.8 billion, generating diluted earnings per share of $2.02, up 29% year-over-year.
Products revenue climbed 18% year-over-year to $78.7 billion, while Services revenue rose 12% to a record $30.7 billion.
Operating cash flow reached a June quarter record of $34.4 billion, and Apple returned $33 billion to shareholders during the quarter.
Paid subscriptions crossed 1.5 billion, and the active installed base reached an all-time high of over 2.5 billion devices.
guidance: Kevan Parekh, CFO, expects Q4 FY2026 total revenue growth of 9% to 11% year-over-year, reflecting a sequential foreign exchange headwind of about 2.5 percentage points.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, projects mid-teens year-over-year revenue growth for iPhone in Q4 FY2026.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, expects Services revenue growth in Q4 FY2026 to track similarly to Q3's 12% before absorbing an approximate 2.5 percentage point sequential foreign exchange drag.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, targets Q4 FY2026 gross margin between 47% and 48%, which includes approximately one percentage point of tariff refund benefit.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, forecasts Q4 FY2026 operating expenses between $19.1 billion and $19.4 billion, and an effective tax rate of around 16.5%.

qa.question: How much of the Q4 revenue deceleration to 9%-11% is due to supply constraints versus foreign exchange, what are the constraints, and will DRAM sourcing flexibility mitigate costs?
qa.answer: The deceleration from June is driven by an approximate 2.5 percentage point sequential foreign exchange drag and significantly widening supply constraints across iPhone, Mac, and iPad, while memory cost inflation will rise further in September despite inventory offsets.

qa.question: What are the adoption expectations for the Apple Upgrade Program, and what are the learnings from the Siri AI beta on compute costs and monetization?
qa.answer: Apple Upgrade remains limited to U.S. retail stores, and while compute cost planning is early, Apple expects heavy Siri AI users will have options to migrate to higher-tier iCloud+ subscriptions.

qa.question: How significantly will supply constraints impact growth in the December quarter, and will Apple broaden silicon sourcing using the Arizona fab?
qa.answer: Apple declined to provide guidance beyond September, attributing current supply tightness to demand exceeding forecasts, while noting the Arizona fab is sourcing over 100 million components this year.

qa.question: What is the pricing philosophy regarding gross profit dollars versus margins, and what factors explain the deceleration in Services growth?
qa.answer: Price adjustments were made reluctantly to manage exponential memory cost spikes holistically across volume and margin, while Services faced foreign exchange headwinds of 2.5 percentage points, mobile gaming softness, link-out transaction rulings, and tough theatrical compares.

qa.question: What regulatory hurdles remain for Siri AI in China and the EU, and how much of the sequential gross margin drop to 46.5% ex-tariffs is memory versus foreign exchange?
qa.answer: Siri AI will ship on Mac in the EU while working with regulators, China approved initial Apple Intelligence features, and more than 100% of the adjusted 160 basis point sequential gross margin drop is caused by memory cost inflation.

unanswered.question: What are the expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program across the install base and its impact on replacement cycles?
unanswered.how: Tim Cook described the leasing mechanics and stated it is currently only available in U.S. retail stores, avoiding adoption metrics or replacement cycle impacts.

exchanges.question: How much of the guided deceleration to 9%-11% revenue growth in September is due to supply constraints versus FX, what are those constraints, and is memory sourcing flexibility intended to mitigate memory inflation or preserve customer value?
exchanges.answer: The deceleration from June is driven by an FX sequential headwind of about 2.5 percentage points and significantly increasing supply constraints sequentially affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad. Memory costs rose sequentially from March to June and will rise further in September, partially offset by carry-in inventory and lower non-memory component costs; having more than the three current DRAM suppliers would help supply and potentially pricing.

exchanges.question: What are the expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program across the install base and its impact on replacement cycles, and what are the learnings from the Siri AI public beta regarding compute costs and monetization via iCloud+?
exchanges.answer: Apple Upgrade offers leasing tailored for customers seeking regular upgrade schedules based on high device residual values; it is currently only in U.S. retail stores. Customer feedback on Siri AI has been overwhelmingly positive, and while compute cost planning is early, Apple expects heavy users will have options to upgrade their tiers on iCloud+.

exchanges.question: How significantly will supply constraints impact the December quarter growth, and is Apple considering broadening silicon providers such as using the Arizona fab to alleviate SoC constraints?
exchanges.answer: Apple is not providing color or guidance beyond September, where the supply crunch is caused by demand outpacing forecasts rather than supplier issues. The Arizona fab is already ramping well, sourcing over 100 million components for Apple this year as part of its $600 billion U.S. commitment.

exchanges.question: What is the thought process and philosophy behind raising prices regarding gross profit dollars versus margins, and what factors explain the deceleration in Services growth into September?
exchanges.answer: Price increases were enacted reluctantly due to a 100-year flood of exponential memory cost increases, balancing units, revenue, and margin holistically rather than by formula. Services growth slowed due to FX, tough compares against last year's theatrical release of the F1 film, softness in mobile gaming, and business model adjustments including link-out transaction rulings, with FX posing a 2.5 percentage point sequential headwind into September.

exchanges.question: Has there been any pull-forward of demand in consumer, enterprise, or education ahead of price hikes, and does AI open up additional long-term addressable markets for Apple?
exchanges.answer: Demand pull-forward is not obvious in the data since iPhone has steadily maintained 22% year-to-date growth, though price elasticity for recent Mac and iPad price hikes is still early to evaluate. On-device AI execution is viewed as a major strategic competitive weapon opening immense future opportunities.

exchanges.question: Will Siri AI increase Apple's capital intensity, and how is the competitive landscape evolving against potential competitor AI devices or bypass technologies?
exchanges.answer: Apple utilizes a hybrid compute model combining internal data centers and third-party cloud, with AI costs impacting both OpEx and COGS, partially offset by potential user migrations to higher iCloud plans. John Ternus reiterated excitement and focus on Apple's internal plans amid industry opportunities.

exchanges.question: What hurdles remain to launch Siri AI in China and the EU, and how much of the guided sequential gross margin moderation to 46.5% excluding tariff refunds is driven by FX versus memory costs?
exchanges.answer: Apple is working with the European Commission to resolve regulations, noting Siri AI will ship on Mac in the EU; China recently approved initial Apple Intelligence features, with Siri AI requiring additional work. For gross margin, more than 100% of the 160 basis point sequential decline to the adjusted 46.5% midpoint is driven by memory cost inflation, with FX having minimal impact.

summary.overview: Chipotle reported second-quarter revenue of $3.3 billion, up 9.3% year-over-year, alongside comparable restaurant sales growth of 2.2%. keyTakeaways: Comparable restaurant sales increased 2.2% in the second quarter, supported by a transaction comp of 1%.
A mid-July softening of about 200 basis points occurred due to industry Cyclospora issues, leading to a Q3 comp guide of around plus 1%.
Digital sales reached $1.3 billion, representing 38.3% of total sales.
The High-Efficiency Equipment Package (HEAP) is driving two to four hours of daily in-restaurant efficiency and improving throughput.

Restaurant level margin was 25.2%, down 220 basis points year-over-year.
Adjusted diluted EPS was flat year-over-year at $0.33.

exchanges.question: What are the incremental costs and expected sales uplifts for store remodels, and have you considered partners in international markets instead of owning?

exchanges.question: What is driving digital sales growth, and are digital sales linked to changes at the register around loyalty and payments?
exchanges.answer: Yes, everything is linked. Launch of Summer of Extras helped inform the rewards refresh, removing friction from the app, and giving greater flexibility on earning and redeeming rewards.

exchanges.question: Should the HEAP rollout be reinvested into labor on the production line, and does it help frontline traffic and customer satisfaction?
exchanges.answer: Yes, about two to four hours of efficiency per day are left in-restaurant for morning prep and peak deployment on the line. This translates to transaction growth, Max 15 throughput improvements, and better food taste scores.

exchanges.question: Why is 350 company-operated openings per year the right level versus 400, and what is gating acceleration?
exchanges.answer: One restaurant per day represents meaningful growth that the organization can handle while developing ready-now leaders. Going beyond 350 could risk diminishing returns or fracturing the base.

exchanges.question: How should we expect the brand positioning to evolve under the new CMO, specifically regarding value and food prep?
exchanges.answer: It is not a 180 pivot but the next evolution of For Real, highlighting fresh in-restaurant food preparation, ingredient usage, and cultivating a better world. Value will focus on extraordinary real ingredients, abundance, speed, and approachable price point.

exchanges.question: Does the 1% Q3 comp guide assume an underlying 3% trend with a sustaining 2% Cyclospora headwind, and what is overall Max 15 throughput?
exchanges.answer: Yes, the 1% guide assumes the 200 bps headwind persists through the quarter. Overall Max 15 throughput is low 20s in-store, mid-teens for digital, and low-to-mid 30s combined per restaurant daily.

exchanges.question: Can you elaborate on in-restaurant loyalty promotion efforts, and do 80% non-scanned transactions correlate with lower income guests?
exchanges.answer: No, they do not over-index with lower income guests; it is more broad-based. In August, a new one-stop pay feature will allow automatic reward points earning upon payment without needing to scan a separate rewards card.

exchanges.question: Can you elaborate on new menu items coming in the months ahead, specifically center of the plate vs sides?
exchanges.answer: Teams are working on center-of-the-plate items, beverage, sides, and desserts. Stage-gated big ideas are being pushed through the process for late 2026 and 2027 calendars.

exchanges.question: What trends were seen in Q2 by age and income, and are any groups improving relative to higher income cohorts?
exchanges.answer: Younger and lower-income cohorts improved the most due to menu innovation like Chipotle Honey Chicken, Cilantro Lime Sauce, and promotions like Matchday BOGO. Q2 also saw highest year-over-year gains in wallet share since 2024.

exchanges.question: What is the margin outlook beyond Q3 regarding the gap between pricing and inflation?

exchanges.question: Were there regional divergences around the World Cup, and what gave comfort to trend towards the higher end of pricing guidance?
exchanges.answer: Restaurants within 10 miles of World Cup stadiums saw a small comp benefit of 50 to 100 bps, but total quarter impact was under 5 bps. Methodical pricing rollout allowed precise resistance measurement and adjustments, providing comfort.

exchanges.question: What incremental color can you provide on LTO contribution to frequency, and do protein LTOs bring in new cohorts or existing guests?
exchanges.answer: LTOs drive transaction lifts from frequent guests coming more often and new guests trying the brand. Protein LTOs bring in new customers who try the brand and increase lifetime value, while current customers visit more frequently.

qa.question: How much are ROEs compressing in E&S casualty given softening, and how are you thinking about broker commissions on a go-forward basis?

exchanges.question: The current year accident year loss ratio improved from Q2 2025. Could you discuss the key factors driving that?
exchanges.answer: Losses for the quarter came in below expectations, representing normal variability and mix of business across a dozen statutory lines. Reserves remain as conservative as ever in the company's history. Regarding reinsurance, the second quarter ceding commission rate is a good indication going forward with a possible slight uptick.

exchanges.question: How much are ROEs compressing in E&S casualty given softening, and how are you thinking about broker commissions on a go-forward basis?
exchanges.answer: Kinsale manages everything to a 20% ROE or greater, with most lines running ahead of that and a 24.4% ROE for the quarter. Brokers maximize economics, and while there is normal soft market tension around gross commissions, Kinsale offers industry-leading customer service, response time, and the broadest risk appetite.

exchanges.question: Does Kinsale view Q2 as the property trough, and what is driving acceleration in the 3.7% growth figure excluding large account property?
exchanges.answer: There is no telling where 2027 property pricing will go due to pressure from various MGAs in London and traditional markets staying heavy in shared layered deals. Heavy competition is also starting to creep into other liability occurrence and long-tail lines like construction and general casualty from London, though pockets of opportunity remain.

exchanges.question: How much of the increase in inbound accounts comes from broker engagement versus competitive pricing, and what is your current view of social inflation and casualty loss trends?
exchanges.answer: The inbound increase is a result of both broker reengagement via the idle broker initiative and pricing. Casualty loss cost trends are estimated at mid-single digits varying by line, and the company has limited social inflation exposure due to smaller accounts and lower limits.

exchanges.question: Can you provide granularity on property pricing in Q2 versus Q1, and how should we think about underlying current accident year loss ratios given mix shifts?
exchanges.answer: Equilibrium will eventually be reached due to intermittent catastrophe losses and disciplined pricing and risk management. Loss ratios could drift up over time, but current bookings feel good and reserves maintain a high level of conservatism. Share buybacks will continue to be the principal capital allocation strategy.

exchanges.question: How has product expansion contributed to growth over the past year, and what is the potential growth uplift going forward?
exchanges.answer: New products and enhancements are never deployed with a feet-first approach, maintaining a crawl, walk, run pace. They are driving submissions and new premium growth at a slow, deliberate pace that will ramp up as the market turns.

summary.overview: Deere reported fiscal Q3 2026 net sales and revenues of $12.608 billion, up 5% year-over-year, alongside net income attributable to Deere & Company of $1.379 billion and diluted EPS of $5.10. Production and Precision Ag net sales declined 6% to $3.998 billion, while Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry grew 12% and 18%, respectively. Management raised full-year guidance in several segments and cited strong precision technology adoption and positive order program trends.
keyTakeaways: Production & Precision Ag and Construction & Forestry are experiencing modest underproduction of a couple percentage points this year due to caution in South America and strong order positions.

Early Order Programs for U.S. and regional large ag are trending up mid-single digits, supported by strong technology take rates such as a doubling of See & Spray usage and 40% adoption of advanced planter technologies.
Construction & Forestry demand remains very positive with four to five months of orders on hand, driven by large infrastructure, data centers, and independent rental channels.
Tariff expectations changed with Section 232 tariff rates dropping from 25% to 15% on imported goods effective June 1st, lowering the full-year direct tariff run rate to $1.1 billion.

summary.overview: Apple Inc. reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16% year-over-year, driven by record June quarter sales across iPhone and Services. Diluted earnings per share increased 29% year-over-year to $2.02, which included a $0.11 per share benefit from a tariff refund. Executive Chairman Tim Cook and CFO Kevan Parekh highlighted expanding supply chain constraints on advanced SoC nodes and rising memory costs as key headwinds for the upcoming quarter.
keyTakeaways: Tim Cook officially transitioned to Executive Chairman, with John Ternus assuming the role of Chief Executive Officer.
iPhone revenue grew 22% year-over-year to a June quarter record of $54.3 billion despite supply constraints.
Supply constraints are intensifying due to high demand exceeding advanced SoC node availability, affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad production.
Rising memory costs impacted June quarter margins and are expected to cause further margin compression in the September quarter.
Apple's active installed base reached an all-time high of over 2.5 billion active devices across all major product categories.
financialHighlights: Total revenue reached $109.4 billion, up 16% year-over-year and setting a new June quarter record.
Gross margin was 50.1%, up 80 basis points150, including an approximate 2 percentage point benefit from a tariff refund.
Services revenue rose 12% year-over-year to $30.7 billion, setting a new June quarter record.
Operating cash flow reached $34.4 billion, a June quarter record, with $33 billion returned to shareholders via buybacks and dividends.
Diluted EPS increased 29% year-over-year to $2.02, supported by a $0.11 per share tariff refund benefit.
guidance: Kevan Parekh, CFO, projects Q4 FY26 total company revenue growth of 9% to 11% year-over-year, incorporating a 2.5 percentage point foreign exchange headwind.

Kevan Parekh, CFO, forecasts Q4 FY26 gross margin between 47% and 48%, which includes an approximate 1 percentage point benefit from a tariff refund.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, anticipates Q4 FY26 operating expenses to range between $19.1 billion and $19.4 billion.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, expects Q4 FY26 tax rate to be approximately 16.5% and OI&E to be around $350 million.

Tim Cook, Executive Chairman, explained that the Apple Upgrade program leverages high residual values to offer affordable device upgrades, while positive beta feedback on Siri AI may lead to higher-tier iCloud+ options for heavy users to offset compute costs.

exchanges.question: How much of the September quarter revenue deceleration is due to supply constraints versus FX, what are the constraints, and is memory sourcing strategy about ensuring supply or preserving customer value?
exchanges.answer: September quarter revenue growth guidance of 9%-11% reflects a 2.5 percentage point sequential FX headwind and significantly increasing supply constraints on iPhone, Mac, and iPad. Constraints are driven by high demand exceeding SoC advanced node availability. Memory costs rose in June and will increase further in September, partially offset by carry-in inventory and lower non-memory BOM costs.

exchanges.question: What are expected adoption rates and impacts of the Apple Upgrade program, and what have you learned from the Siri AI public beta regarding demand and compute cost recovery through iCloud+?
exchanges.answer: Apple Upgrade is a leasing program available in U.S. retail stores leveraging high residual values to offer affordable device upgrades, with positive early feedback. Public and developer beta feedback for Siri AI has been overwhelmingly positive. Heavy users may be offered higher-tier iCloud+ upgrade options to offset compute costs.

exchanges.question: How significantly will supply constraints impact the December quarter, and could Apple expand silicon sourcing with partners like the Arizona fab to alleviate supply limitations?
exchanges.answer: Apple is not providing guidance or color beyond the September quarter. The supply constraints are caused by strong product demand for iPhone and Mac exceeding forecasts rather than supplier issues. Apple sources over 100 million components from Arizona this year as part of its $600 billion U.S. commitment.

exchanges.question: What is the philosophy behind recent product price increases, and what factors are driving the sequential deceleration in services growth?
exchanges.answer: Price increases were enacted reluctantly due to exponential memory cost inflation, evaluating units, revenue, and margins holistically over the long term. Services growth slowed due to FX headwinds, lack of an F1 film release compare, and mobile gaming softness in the App Store. FX will present a 2.5 percentage point sequential headwind to services in Q4.

exchanges.question: Are you seeing any pull-forward of demand ahead of price increases, and does edge AI open new long-term addressable market opportunities for Apple?
exchanges.answer: There is no evidence of demand pull-forward in the 22% year-to-date iPhone growth, though price elasticity from recent Mac and iPad price increases will take time to measure. AI presents massive long-term opportunities for Apple, with Siri AI and on-device processing offering major competitive advantages.

exchanges.question: Will Siri AI change Apple's capital intensity, and how does management view the evolving AI hardware competitive landscape?
exchanges.answer: Apple utilizes a hybrid model combining internal data centers and third-party cloud infrastructure. Higher AI investments across OpEx and COGS may be partially offset long term by iCloud+ tier upgrades. John Ternus expressed confidence in Apple's plan and execution in the evolving AI landscape.

exchanges.question: What are the regulatory hurdles for launching Siri AI in Europe and China, and what is the breakdown of the sequential gross margin decrease?
exchanges.answer: Apple is working with the European Commission to launch Siri AI (Mac Siri AI is supported), while initial Apple Intelligence features received approval in China with Siri AI approvals still ahead. The sequential gross margin drop to 46.5% (adjusted midpoint) for Q4 is more than 100% explained by rising memory costs, offset partially by carry-in inventory and lower non-memory BOM costs.

summary.overview: JPMorgan Chase reported net income of $16.9 billion, diluted EPS of $6.14, and an ROTCE of 23% for the second quarter of 2026. Firm revenue rose 15% year-on-year ex-significant items, driven by a 27% increase in CIB revenue and an 86% jump in Equities trading. In response to strong first-half trading outperformance and deposit mix, management raised full-year guidance across net interest income and adjusted expenses.
keyTakeaways: JPMorgan raised full-year 2026 total NII guidance to approximately $105.5 billion, reflecting NII ex-Markets of about $96.5 billion and Markets NII of about $9 billion.
Full-year 2026 adjusted expenses were revised upward by $2.5 billion to about $107.5 billion, with $1.5 billion already incurred in the first half to support capital markets outperformance.
The board elevated Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to co-presidents, while Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, stated his multi-year succession timetable has not changed.
Equities trading revenue surged 86% year-on-year, propelled by dynamic Asian flows, South Korean market dynamics, large IPO activity, and index rebalancing.
Card net charge-off expectations improved to approximately 3.2% for the full year, down from the prior approximately 3.4% guide.
financialHighlights: Firm net income was $16.9 billion, yielding diluted EPS of $6.14 and an ROTCE of 23%.
Non-interest expenses rose 15% year-on-year to $27.3 billion.

exchanges.question: What should investors think about the elevation of Doug and Troy to co-presidents and its implications for Dimon's CEO tenure? Also, how sustainable is the strength across IB and markets, and how risk-on is the firm?
exchanges.answer: The board elevated two co-presidents to prepare them to do far more, Marianne decided to retire upon learning the plans, and Dimon's tenure timetable has not changed. Barnum added that IB saw deal pull-forward but pipelines remain robust, while equities strength was driven by specific dynamic conditions unlikely to repeat exactly, noting the broader market is risk-on while JPM seeks to support clients cautiously.

exchanges.question: How are higher-for-longer rates impacting progression toward the 15% retail deposit market share target? Also, where is JPM in its expense investment cycle regarding medium-term operating leverage?
exchanges.answer: Wholesale deposits outperformed in the first half partly from BFI and data center lending, while consumer deposit growth remains guided to low single-digits with strong checking growth balancing yield-seeking flows, keeping the 15% long-term market share goal intact. On expenses, investments in branches, AI, and bankers remain an ongoing continuation of historical strategy to build future returns while delivering high current returns.

exchanges.question: What is driving the upward revision to NII ex-Markets and the expected exit run rate? What is driving the increase in markets NII despite a higher rate outlook?
exchanges.answer: The revision of NII ex-Markets to $96.5 billion is driven primarily by higher deposit balances across wholesale and consumer and favorable mix shifts, alongside modestly higher rates. Markets NII raised to about $9 billion because the liability-sensitivity drag is being overwhelmed by balance sheet composition changes (fewer non-interest-bearing financed assets) and a roughly $150 million shift of equity/NII allocated from corporate to CIB.

exchanges.question: What characteristics is the board seeking in a successor, and does the recent restructuring mean Jamie Dimon's tenure is more fixed or still rolling?
exchanges.answer: The succession timetable remains unchanged at several or a few years and is entirely up to the board. The board seeks leaders with analytical power, grit, heart, work ethic, and ability to manage 300,000 global staff across branches, call centers, and executive levels, highlighting deep executive bench strength including co-presidents, Jen Piepszak, and Mary Erdoes.

exchanges.question: Could intermediate-term expense growth slow and operating leverage become more achievable due to tech/AI? Also, what is the latest update on regulatory proposals like Basel III and the G-SIB surcharge?
exchanges.answer: Dimon rejected the premise of pursuing perpetual operating leverage when margins and returns are high, though expense growth could potentially slow in 2027 or 2028, noting AI benefits ultimately accrue to customers via competition rather than permanently boosting bank margins. On regulation, Dimon urged eliminating double-counting of operational risk and market risk capital, recalibrating G-SIB scores back to 2015 standards, and Barnum argued against proposed short-term wholesale funding rules that penalize full-service banks serving Main Street.

exchanges.question: Is the current environment as good as it gets, and is there a tipping point where deposit betas and volumes change sharply under higher rates?
exchanges.answer: Conditions are close to as good as it gets, though how long they will last is unknown. Barnum explained that while negative convexity in deposit rates has not yet materialized in this cycle, the firm stresses for accelerated rate paid and franchise defense in extreme rate scenarios such as a 7% environment rather than naively relying on current empirical EAR.

exchanges.question: Why describe this as as good as it gets if marginal revenue flow-through is roughly 77%? Also, what qualifies Troy to run the consumer bank given his background as a trader?
exchanges.answer: Dimon explained the market is exuberant and healthy, making further improvement hard to predict. Barnum clarified that of the $2.5 billion expense guidance raise, $1.5 billion was already incurred in the first half to support $6.5 billion in capital markets revenue outperformance. Dimon defended Troy's transition to consumer by citing his executive EQ, analytical skills, and broad operational and technology leadership in IB and markets, with Barnum noting Troy was an options trader.

exchanges.question: Could banks use AI to become structurally leaner and downsize headcount, and what specific factors drove the exceptional equities quarter that cannot be repeated?
exchanges.answer: AI has nearly 1,000 use cases currently with 50 primary ones, and while it will drive major efficiencies and job retraining (having already cut headcount by 30-40% in discrete units), competition ensures benefits accrue mostly to clients. Barnum clarified equities outperformance was driven by a rare confluence of large IPOs, index rebalancing, South Korean market dynamics, and heavy Asia cash and derivatives flow.

exchanges.question: What is Main Street consumer resilience and CapEx breadth showing? Also, why repurchase shares at 3x tangible book instead of hoarding capital or pursuing M&A?
exchanges.answer: Consumer spending and credit remain solid with delinquencies below expectations, with CapEx seeing strong demand across data centers, AI, and infrastructure. On buybacks, Barnum and Dimon noted excess capital of around $40 billion will be deployed organically given massive global funding needs across security, infrastructure, and defense at targeted 17% returns, though opportunistic inorganic options remain evaluated.

exchanges.question: What is the rollout status for the smart cash tool, and what is the overarching strategy for European consumer digital banking?
exchanges.answer: The smart cash tool is in test cases targeting a narrow client segment competing for deposits and investments, with rollouts occurring this year. In Europe, Chase UK has 2.5 to 3 million customers and the Berlin/German launch is ahead of expectations, with plans to expand investment and credit card products to scale a pan-European digital bank.

exchanges.question: Are competitors showing underwriting excesses in credit, and could bank regulation enter a period of stability that enhances valuations?
exchanges.answer: Barnum observed aggressive underwriting in areas like data center power supply and tenant risk, while Dimon noted mild deterioration via loose expense add-backs, PIK, weaker covenants, and rollover risk across certain peers. On regulation, Barnum favored stable risk standards over shifting constraints, while Dimon criticized regulatory double counts and ineffective resolution planning, hoping for a refocus on true safety and soundness.

exchanges.question: Are tech and marketing expenses being pulled forward, what is token expense impact, and are there limits to increasing CIB capital allocations?
exchanges.answer: Barnum stated token expense is trivial for the full year though accelerating in the second half, and JPM focuses on matching the right AI models to tasks rather than overpaying for cutting-edge models. Capital allocations to CIB are driven by client demand and market volatility rather than fixed hedge-fund-like budgets, with ample excess capital to deploy, while liquidity regulation remains the key system constraint.

exchanges.question: How are deposits progressing toward the 15% retail market share target, and where is the firm in the investment cycle regarding operating leverage?

exchanges.question: What drove the upward revision to NII ex-Markets guidance, and why is markets NII guidance higher despite higher rate expectations?

exchanges.question: What traits is the board seeking in a future CEO, and does Marianne Lake's departure imply an extension of CEO tenure?

exchanges.question: Could AI slow expense growth to create operating leverage over the intermediate term, and is there any update on regulatory capital proposal adjustments?

exchanges.question: Is current cross-segment performance as good as it gets, and could higher interest rates hit a tipping point that changes consumer deposit behavior?

exchanges.question: Can AI enable a structural reduction in bank operating costs, and what specific drivers elevated equities performance this quarter?

Barnum attributed equities strength to major IPOs, index rebalancing, Asian market activity, and Korean market dynamics.

exchanges.question: What are you observing across consumer health and CapEx, and what is the logic behind share buybacks at 3x tangible book value versus organic or inorganic capital deployment?

exchanges.question: What is the status of the smart cash tool rollout, and what is the long-term objective for European consumer banking expansion?

exchanges.question: Are competitors showing credit underwriting excesses, and could a stable regulatory environment emerge to support bank valuations?

exchanges.question: How does Lilly envision expanding consumer treatment opportunities in obesity, and how does the U.S. compare to the international self-pay market?
exchanges.answer: Obesity utilization remains in the mid-single digits globally, representing substantial upside. In the U.S., access has expanded via the Medicare Bridge Program and state Medicaid, while about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions remain in self-pay. Outside the U.S., obesity is primarily out-of-pocket, prompting Lilly to adapt and launch international versions of LillyDirect within local regulatory frameworks.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities

exchanges.question: What is driving the slower U.S. launch curve for Foundayo and when will it inflect, plus what are the competitive dynamics and share trends ex-U.S. against Novo Nordisk?
exchanges.answer: U.S. progress focuses on physician education, expanded access—including CVS adding Foundayo in June and the Medicare Bridge launch on July 1—and DTC marketing. In the last week of July, volume nearly doubled compared to a month prior, with new starts representing about one in four patients. Ex-U.S., early UAE signals show incretin-naive patient adoption and steady Lilly market share; upcoming launches in Saudi Arabia and Mexico will precede broad 2027 rollouts, with no supply gating.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities

exchanges.question: What are the requirements, milestones, and status of securing a BLA filing pathway with the FDA for retatrutide?
exchanges.answer: Lilly maintains retatrutide qualifies as a biologic under the amino acid count rule and protein analogy, despite a mixed initial court ruling amid active litigation. Clinical data packages are complete, but additional CMC data is being gathered ahead of an anticipated Q1 2027 submission while discussions with the FDA continue.

exchanges.question: What are the initial rollout trends, surprises, and oral versus injectable split under the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Program?
exchanges.answer: The program has expanded obesity therapy access to approximately 35% more Americans, with prior authorization processes operating smoothly and LillyDirect integrated for fulfillment. Prescriptions skew heavily toward injectables at around 80%, and an estimated 60% to 70% of participants represent new patients previously without access.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities

exchanges.question: Does Lilly need a commercial strategy to protect retatrutide against existing market alternatives, and what new indications does its higher efficacy enable beyond diabesity?
exchanges.answer: Lilly expects patients will embrace authentic, approved product upon availability. Its efficacy enables opportunities like osteoarthritis knee pain, where TRIUMPH trials showed pain reductions of 75%, an ongoing study in MASH/MASLD leveraging the glucagon mechanism, and an ongoing chronic lower back pain study reading out in 2027.

exchanges.question: What is Lilly's post-Verzenio strategy in breast cancer, and is an all-oral combination involving SERD and oral PI3K on the table?
exchanges.answer: Lilly targets the estrogen receptor, CDK4/6, and PI3 kinase alpha, aiming to combine therapies across all three. The phase III trial for the PI3K inhibitor tersolisib will begin soon in combination with endocrine therapies and CDK4/6 (principally Verzenio), with plans to ultimately combine it with imlunestrant (INLURIYO) in an all-oral regimen.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development

exchanges.question: Does full-year guidance imply a second-half revenue deceleration versus Q2 despite new access programs, and is this conservatism or driven by price?
exchanges.answer: Second-half growth compares against a high H2 2025 base that included the initial launch bolus of MOUNJARO across international markets, while Q2 2026 benefited from one-off pre-period rebate and discount adjustments. Additionally, the second-half outlook reflects standard European Q3 vacation seasonality and U.S. Q4 Type 2 diabetes seasonality.

exchanges.question: Which international regions are driving MOUNJARO growth, and what are the competitive observations regarding generic semaglutide launches in markets like India?
exchanges.answer: International growth is driven by China—reaching category leadership 16 months post-NRDL—as well as Korea, the U.K., Mexico, and Germany. In India, Brazil, and Canada, tirzepatide prescriptions continued to expand following generic semaglutide introductions, supported by clinical differentiation and generic supply constraints.

exchanges.question: How extensive is the U.S. Foundayo sampling program, and how significantly has the prescriber base expanded?
exchanges.answer: Lilly is providing full 30-day initial dose samples across the prescriber base similar to retail oral small molecules, supported by adequate inventory. The prescriber base has expanded from approximately 8,000 at the prior quarter's earnings call to 36,000 prescribers.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities

exchanges.question: How sustainable is the net price premium in obesity, how much does medical exception drive it, and will the return of CVS formulary access lower realized net price?
exchanges.answer: Net price dynamics reflect clear channel pricing—from LillyDirect direct-to-patient ($299 to $449) and the Bridge program ($245) to commercial contracts—alongside script size effects. Restoring open CVS access in Q4 will transition patients away from medical exceptions, leading to expected lower net price per unit that will be more than offset by volume expansion and is already factored into guidance.

exchanges.question: Is Lilly seeking to build scalable franchises in psychiatry and vaccines, or are recent acquisitions opportunistic, one-off scientific investments?
exchanges.answer: Both therapy areas share immense unmet medical need, allowing Lilly to acquire compelling technologies at disciplined valuations. Future investments in psychiatry and infectious diseases will remain opportunistic based on asset availability and shareholder value creation rather than a rigid target build-out.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development

exchanges.question: Which specific non-obesity pipeline programs should investors pay closer attention to?
exchanges.answer: Key programs include gene editing for PCSK9 (VERVE-102) and oral/injectable Lp(a) assets in cardiometabolic, orexin agonist cleminorexton in neuroscience, Kelonia in vivo CAR T (KLN-1010) and Ajax type II JAK inhibitor (AJ1-11095) in oncology, and expanding indications and novel combinations in immunology.

exchanges.question: What is the global commercial potential for Foundayo in obesity given UAE performance, and will oral delivery improve ex-U.S. government reimbursement in diabetes compared to tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: UAE results show initial demand among incretin-naive patients, though early numbers include launch inventory stocking before major 2027 rollouts. For Type 2 diabetes, orforglipron's head-to-head clinical data package and small-molecule profile offer a compelling value proposition for reimbursement, though launch focus will center first on chronic weight management.

exchanges.answer: We believe we have the best medicines for the estrogen receptor, CDK4/6, and PI3 kinase alpha targets, and we plan to combine them all. We are beginning the phase III program for tersolisib, which will initially be combined with existing endocrine therapies, and we envision combining it with INLURIYO down the road.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development

exchanges.question: Is your guidance implying a deceleration in revenue versus Q2 for the back half of the year, or is there something we are missing on price?
exchanges.answer: The guidance factors in pre-period adjustments for rebates and discounts in the U.S. that we do not expect to continue into the second half. Additionally, the base period in 2025 included a bolus of MOUNJARO launches that will not repeat, and we also factor in typical Q3 European seasonality and Q4 U.S. Type 2 diabetes seasonality.

exchanges.question: Which specific regions are seeing the most growth for the OUS launch, and what are you seeing in India with generic semaglutide launching?
exchanges.answer: We are seeing significant growth in China, Korea, the U.K., Mexico, and Germany, taking market leadership in many places. In India and Brazil, MOUNJARO prescriptions continue to grow even after the launch of generic semaglutide, driven by our strong superiority data.

exchanges.question: How extensive is your sampling program for Foundayo, and what are you seeing regarding the U.S. prescribing base expansion?
exchanges.answer: We are incorporating sampling for the first 30 days of the first dose, similar to typical oral small molecules in the retail market. Our prescriber base has increased from 8,000 to 36,000 prescribers, and we continue to see week-on-week growth.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities

exchanges.question: How sustainable is the medical exception dynamic driving net pricing for obesity, especially given CVS is back on formulary?
exchanges.answer: Medical exceptions are a driver, but script size also impacts the commercial segment price. We view medical exceptions as a short-term situation and expect the price to go down as we achieve open access, which is embedded in our guidance and will be offset by volume growth.

exchanges.question: Do you see psychiatry and vaccines as areas Lilly can scale, or are these assets more one-off based on intriguing science?
exchanges.answer: These areas share immense unmet need, and we saw opportunities to acquire impactful technology at disciplined prices. We will remain opportunistic based on what is available for acquisition and partnering rather than committing to specific future builds in these areas.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development

exchanges.question: Are there specific pipeline assets outside of obesity that you are really excited about and think the street should pay more attention to?
exchanges.answer: We are excited about our cardiovascular efforts with PCSK9 gene editing and Lp(a)-lowering drugs, as well as neuroscience programs in sleep-wake disorders and major depressive disorder. In oncology, we have a rich period of readouts and new molecules like the Kelonia in vivo CAR T and the Ajax JAK inhibitor.

exchanges.question: How do you see the potential for Foundayo ex-U.S. for obesity, and do you think it will be better reimbursed than tirzepatide for diabetes?
exchanges.answer: There is a significant opportunity as the majority of patients are naive to incretin treatments, with major OUS rollouts planned for early 2027. We are likely better positioned for Type 2 reimbursement with an oral given the strong head-to-head trial data, though reimbursement always takes time.

summary.overview: Chipotle Mexican Grill reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $3.3 billion, an increase of 9.3% year-over-year, supported by comparable restaurant sales growth of 2.2% and transaction comps of 1.0%. Restaurant-level margin compressed 220 basis points year-over-year to 25.2%, and adjusted diluted EPS remained flat at $0.33. Adam Rymer, CFO, guided full-year comparable restaurant sales to the low single-digit range and anticipated Q3 comps around plus 1%, reflecting an estimated 200 basis point headwind from an industry-wide Cyclospora issue.
keyTakeaways: Comp sales increased 2.2% in Q2, led by a 1.0% transaction comp and a 1.6% menu pricing contribution.
Late July trends softened by approximately 200 basis points due to an industry Cyclospora issue, leading management to guide Q3 comps to around plus 1%.
Digital sales expanded to $1.3 billion, representing 38.3% of total revenue compared to 35.5% in the prior-year period.
Chipotle opened 101 new restaurants during the quarter, including 80 Chipotlanes and one international partner-operated store.
Management reiterated a full-year target of approximately 350 restaurant openings and roughly 2,000 High-Efficiency Equipment Package (HEAP) installations.
financialHighlights: Total revenue reached $3.3 billion, representing 9.3% growth year-over-year.
Adjusted diluted EPS was flat year-over-year at $0.33.
Restaurant-level margin declined 220 basis points year-over-year to 25.2%.
Cost of sales rose about 80 basis points to 29.7%, labor costs grew 30 basis points to 25.0%, and other operating costs rose 90 basis points to 14.9%.
The company repurchased $631 million of common stock during Q2 at an average price of $32.55 per share, leaving $800 million in cash and investments.
